title: How House Swapping Works
summary: Josh and Chuck explain house swapping, where travelers exchange homes rather than paying for hotels. They open with the Kyle MacDonald red paper clip-to-house story (Kipling, Saskatchewan, with Corbin Burnett's snow globe trade) as a tangent, then cover the three types: traditional simultaneous exchanges, non-simultaneous (credit-banking) swaps, and hospitality exchanges (staying with or hosting strangers, e.g., CouchSurfing). They discuss origins in 1993 with Intervac, practical preparation such as letters of agreement, insurance checks, leaving notes for breakage, pets, and valuables, and sites like HomeLink and Intervac listings. The episode closes with a COED fall fundraiser announcement in Atlanta and a listener mail segment.

segments.title: Opening banter and red paper clip story
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck banter, then Josh recounts Kyle MacDonald trading a red paper clip up to a house in Kipling, Saskatchewan, which the town then resold after the trade; Chuck ties it to the topic of house swapping.

segments.title: What house swapping is and its growth
segments.summary: Chuck explains house swapping as home exchange, says it dates to the mid-1950s and is growing, and they contrast it with hospitality exchanges, noting the hosts' comfort levels.

segments.title: Three types of home swaps
segments.summary: They describe traditional simultaneous exchanges, non-simultaneous swaps where credits are banked (illustrated with a Rio example), and hospitality exchanges where hosts and guests share the home, with the hosts saying they would be uncomfortable with the latter.

segments.title: Hospitality exchanges and CouchSurfing
segments.summary: The hosts discuss hospitality exchanges in more depth, including sharing a home with strangers and showing guests around town, and point listeners to CouchSurfing.com for those who want that style.

segments.title: Who swaps and preparing the exchange
segments.summary: They note most swappers are professionals and that it is not like couch surfing. They outline the planning details swappers exchange: car use, plants, pets, mail, house quirks, and keys, and mention neighbors as local contacts.

segments.title: Etiquette, the 1993 origin, and common complaints
segments.summary: Advice on treating the other home well, such as leaving notes for broken items and restocking the fridge. They cite the 1993 founding of Intervac by teachers as the origin, and discuss expectation mismatches like cleanliness.

segments.title: Letter of agreement and insurance
segments.summary: They describe a letter of agreement, which is not a legal contract, outlining phone and internet charges, who may stay, damage handling, and checking homeowners, renters, or auto insurance for caveats.

segments.title: Swap sites and screening tips
segments.summary: They mention Intervac, HomeLink, and other listing sites ranging from free Craigslist to paid memberships. They suggest trusting intuition, asking for references, watching for controlling hosts, and securing valuables.

segments.title: Sponsor and COED announcement
segments.summary: Hosts promote a COED fall fiesta in Alpharetta, Georgia, on October 21, which raises money for textbooks for Guatemalan schools.

segments.title: Listener mail and sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts answer listener questions on favorite soda, a Fight question, the podcast's future, use of innuendo, hardest episodes to explain, and American vs Mexican Coke, then sign off.
